pressure.en: Force spread over an area. In espresso: how hard the water pushes on the puck. 1 bar is roughly the air pressure at sea level; 9 bar is nine times that.

resistance.en: How strongly something opposes flow. A fine, tightly tamped puck has high hydraulic resistance; a heater coil has electrical resistance.

flow.en: How much water moves per second (ml/s or g/s). Flow ≈ pressure ÷ resistance.

boiler.en: The small metal tank with a heating element that heats the water. On the E24 it is brass.

vibratory pump.en: A pump with an electromagnet that shakes a small piston back and forth many times a second. Cheap, compact and noisy.

OPV.en: Over-pressure valve. A spring-loaded valve that dumps extra water back to the tank once pressure passes its set point.

three-way valve.en: An electrically-driven (solenoid) valve with three ports. Powered: boiler → group head. Unpowered: group head → drip tray, which releases pressure and dries the puck.

solenoid.en: A coil of wire that becomes a magnet when current flows, pulling a metal plunger. Used to open and close valves.

thermostat.en: A switch that opens or closes at a set temperature. Here a bimetal disc snaps open when hot and closes when it cools.

hysteresis.en: When a switch turns off at one value but back on at a different value, so the system cycles in a band rather than holding one point.

PID.en: Proportional–integral–derivative control. A controller that sets heater power from how far off the target you are, how long you have been off, and how fast you are moving.

SSR.en: Solid-state relay. A switch with no moving parts: a small low-voltage signal turns a mains-voltage load (the heater) on and off silently.

thermocouple.en: Two different metals joined at a tip. Heat the tip and a tiny voltage appears, which a circuit converts to temperature.

Seebeck effect.en: A temperature difference across a junction of two different conductors produces a voltage. This is what makes thermocouples work.

transducer.en: A device that turns one kind of signal into another. A pressure transducer turns water pressure into a voltage the board can read.

duty cycle.en: The fraction of time something is switched on. A 1200 W heater on 25% of the time delivers 300 W on average.

preinfusion.en: Wetting the puck gently at low pressure for a few seconds before full pressure, so water spreads evenly.

extraction yield.en: The share of the dry coffee dose that ended up dissolved in your cup. EY = TDS × drink mass ÷ dose.

Eco PCB.en: A small circuit board on EU 230/240 V Gaggias that switches the machine off after a period of inactivity, to meet EU standby rules.

thermal fuse.en: A one-shot safety part. If it gets too hot it breaks the circuit for good and must be replaced.

neutral.en: The return wire of a mains circuit. Line (L) carries the voltage; neutral (N) completes the loop.

line.en: The live wire of a mains circuit, at 230 V relative to neutral in Bulgaria.

channeling.en: When water finds an easy crack through the puck and rushes through it, under-extracting the rest.

jumper.en: A short wire that connects two points so current bypasses whatever used to sit between them.
